source_quote: "One agent, one branch, one directory, zero collisions." (jamilxt, dev.to); the author also writes "I have not run these exact three-agent sessions myself." Evidence, Claude Code docs (worktrees): "Running each Claude Code session in its own worktree gives it a separate copy of the files to edit, so one session can build a feature while a second fixes a bug."
source_note: Approved by Sebi 20 Nov 2026 (PROTOCOL.md, Module 7 entry). Module 7 rules = private/m5/RULES.md 'Runs' plus private/m7/DESIGN.md 'Decisions (Sebi, 20 Nov 2026)': day 63 keeps Core 3 (t1, t2, t3) and runs 3 batches per arm (9 graded tasks a side), Haiku 4.5 on every side, Claude Code 2.1.309 pinned by LAB_CLAUDE_BIN=~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.309, config dir ~/.claude-lab (claude.ai skill and plugin sync off), CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 on every side, standard verdict rule, three numbers before each run (pass rate, the behaviour count below, cost per passed run), the habit measured first, an agent reads every transcript, private/m7/tools/preflight.py run on the smoke and day events. allowed_tools_extra: earlier t2/h2 days added nothing because the runner's base list already covers the tasks' real commands (pnpm --filter <pkg> build/test, npx vitest, npx tsc, node); extras below exist only where the trick needs them. Design, kill switches and pilots: private/m7/DESIGN.md, RISKS.md. Unit = a batch; verdict = the pre-registered wall-time rule in PROTOCOL.md (Module 7 entry), applied by batch.py.
verdict_rule: Per side: pass count = graded tasks passed out of 9; time = mean wall minutes per batch (copy start to last agent exit, grading and sequential snapshots excluded); cost = mean summed cost per batch. Then the standard decide() rule with these in place of avg_minutes and avg_cost_usd. Infrastructure: a batch with any infra error is rerun; 2 or more rerun batches on an arm = inconclusive.
behaviour_count: Merge conflicts when combining the 3 worktree branches (git merge-tree); pnpm install minutes per worktree; peak memory
habit_measure: The sequential arm's wall minutes per batch
kill_switches: pnpm install --offline fails in a worktree: APFS-clone each package's node_modules instead and say install cost is excluded
Any batch with an infrastructure error: rerun the batch
Anything else heavy running on the machine during a batch: rerun the batch

with.label: Parallel: 3 worktrees, pnpm install --offline in each, t1/t2/t3 headless at once, then merge-tree

without.label: Sequential: one folder, t1 then t2 then t3, fresh session each, snapshot after each
